note: Hand-written expected answers. The pipeline is broken if it misses these. Every entry states date_precision explicitly on both the input claim and the expected verification, because precision is itself a claim: a source attesting '1985' has not attested '1985-01-01', and padding it would manufacture agreement or disagreement that no source expressed.

precision_contract.rule: claim.date_precision and expect.date.precision must each match the granularity of their own date string. A verifier must never return a precision finer than the sources support.

claim.description: A PUMA 560 was used to position a needle for a stereotactic neurosurgical biopsy.
ROBODOC performed femoral canal preparation in a human total hip arthroplasty.

entity_aliases: Automated Endoscopic System for Optimal Positioning
claim.description: AESOP received FDA 510(k) clearance as an endoscope positioner.

date.note: Bimodal across a year boundary. The mechanism is unconfirmed — see README, 'Pending empirical checks'. One candidate is openFDA's own record, where date_received and decision_date can straddle a new year and secondary sources cite whichever they saw. Precision stays 'year' because neither mode is attested more finely.

event_type.note: The event type is not in doubt — a 510(k) is a clearance. Only the date is contested. This is the §6.2 case that whole-claim verification cannot see.
Must resolve to regulatory_approval, distinct from the 1992 first clinical use and from AESOP's clearance.

claim.description: The da Vinci Surgical System received FDA premarket approval for general laparoscopic surgery.

date.note: The only month-precision entry in the set. A verifier that coarsens this to '2000' has lost information the sources carry; one that reports a specific day has invented it.

claim.description: Supervised autonomous robotic soft tissue surgery was reported in Science Translational Medicine.

conflation.note: Must NOT be conflated with the 2022 entry despite the shared acronym. If entity drift is detected across these two, it should surface on entity, not date.

claim.description: Autonomous laparoscopic robotic anastomosis was reported in Science Robotics.

conflation.note: 'Smart Tissue Autonomous Robot' (2022) and 'Smart Tissue Anastomosis Robot' (2016) are materially different systems. §6.6 acronym drift: the alias expansions differ, which is entity drift and produces false corroboration if missed.

negative.note: REQUIRED. If this returns corroborated, verification is not working and no other feature matters (§8).

claim.description: ROBODOC was the first surgical robot approved by the FDA.

date.note: 1992 is ROBODOC's first clinical use, not its approval date; the PMA is 2008. The date is attached to the wrong event.

superlative.note: §6.3: any competing claimant with sources makes this contested, full stop, regardless of how many sources back the original.

competing_claimants.note: Cleared via 510(k), not approved via PMA. The conflation of clearance with approval is what generates the competing 'first FDA-approved' claims.

conflation.note: regulatory_clearance and regulatory_approval merged under one label across sources.
